sources.entry: Bitcoin Core - Official Bitcoin Core software for running a full Bitcoin node.

summary.one_liner: Bitcoin Core is the reference software for running a full Bitcoin node that downloads and validates blocks and transactions from the Bitcoin peer-to-peer network.
summary.what_it_does: Connects to the Bitcoin peer-to-peer network to download and fully validate blocks and transactions. Includes a wallet and an optional graphical user interface, which can be built in. Further documentation is in the doc folder. The README is primarily a development-process document for this integration/staging tree: it describes the master branch as regularly built and tested but not guaranteed stable, with tags marking official releases. It explains the testing approach, which uses ctest for unit tests and a Python test_runner.py for functional tests, plus CI on Windows, Linux, and macOS. It also covers manual QA and translations, which are submitted through Transifex rather than GitHub pull requests.
how_to_run: For a binary release, see the official Bitcoin Core downloads (the README link is missing from the text)
Run unit tests with: ctest (in the build directory)
Run functional tests with: build/test/functional/test_runner.py (assuming build is your build directory)
notable: Full node that independently validates blocks and transactions
Includes an optional built-in wallet and graphical interface
Unit tests via ctest and Python regression/integration tests
CI runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS
Translations managed through Transifex, not GitHub pull requests
caveats: Master branch is not guaranteed to be completely stable; use tagged releases for stable versions
Build instructions are in separate doc files rather than the README
The README describes the repository as a development tree, so it is not primarily an end-user download page
